threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look shocked when the bus driver shouts at someone for not having their Oyster card ready. We’ve all been there.
Caught the 381 last night; a bloke was serenading the driver with some old Elvis tunes. Didn’t skip a beat even as we hit bumps. Classic Bermondsey moment.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: One day, I saw a guy in a full dinosaur costume waiting for the bus at Sonnenallee. It hit me—this is home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can catch a party in a former factory on a Thursday night, then grab a döner for breakfast before 10 AM. That’s pure Berlin life.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they instinctively look for the BART delays before heading to the game – not just the schedule.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus stuck behind a food truck making a burrito delivery at 3 AM. Driver’s patience was impressive, let alone the hungry riders aboard.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every corner in Gràcia is Instagram-worthy, but they miss the hidden life in the alleys where locals sip café and share stories.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still googling directions at the metro station instead of just asking a vendor in the square.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot a newbie from a mile away; they still think ‘the bus’ actually gets you anywhere on time.
Heard a guy on the 35 last night trying to offer his mixtape to anyone who'd listen. Had a surprisingly solid sound, but he was relentless.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: One morning, I spotted a flock of pigeons nestled on a toddler's tricycle outside the Kiez-Kiosk, like they owned the place. That’s when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you'll find spontaneous street parties on a Tuesday evening, complete with DJs and impromptu dance-offs. It's like the city just decides to celebrate life.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they can name the day of the week just by BART's moods—like when Civic Center's shut down for a loud bang at rush hour.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full suit trying to catch the bus while juggling a burrito and a coffee. Classic Mission moment—where work and tacos collide.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about the parks and plazas, but it's the quiet backstreets with those little artisan shops that give it life.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by their fascination with the tiled floors in cafes, snapping photos like it's an art installation. Classic rookie move.
